speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) how many Advance Medical Directives (AMDs) have been registered to date; and (b) to make it easier to sign an AMD, whether the Ministry will consider removing the requirement that AMDs must always be signed before a doctor, even when there are no concerns that the individual may lack mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Ministry will reassess the need to continue prohibiting doctors from asking their patients if they have an AMD, especially as the Registrar of AMDs is contactable during office or clinic hours, and doctors may otherwise experience difficulties ascertaining their patient's AMD status if the certification of terminal illness occurs after the Registrar's regular office hours.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The decision to make an AMD must be taken seriously as it is a legal document stating that an individual does not want to use any life-sustaining treatment to prolong his life in the event that he is terminally ill, unconscious or requires life-sustaining treatment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Hence, safeguards are in place to protect the interests of individuals.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, a witnessing doctor ensures that the individual understands the medical implications of making an AMD, is not being coerced and is of sound mind.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Strict confidentiality of AMDs are maintained to ensure that the knowledge of an AMD does not inappropriately influence treatment decisions before a patient is certified terminally ill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have established operational processes to ensure that AMD search requests made by doctors receive prompt attention, including after regular office hours.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: By way of supplementary question, I would like to ask if the Minister of State will agree that, in general, the take-up rate for AMDs has been quite slow compared to Lasting Power of Attorney (LPAs).

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: I am glad to see that the numbers have now been boosted to 84,000, but I know it is had a very, very long roll-out, bearing in mind that this legislation is now 30 years old.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: I accept that what the Minister of State has said, that it is good for those who want to sign an AMD to get advice from their doctors on the implications.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: But I will make the argument that lawyers, too, are able to give the same advice, of course, provided that the individual has mental capacity and there is no issue of their lack of understanding.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: The advantage of being able to remove this requirement that one of the witnesses must be a doctor will mean that those who are interested to make end-of-life decision-making will have a one-stop shop, they will be able to see the lawyers, and have both their LPAs and their AMDs signed at the same time and have access to the advice to make informed decisions.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: So, I hope this is something that the Ministry is open to doing – to remove the requirement that one of the witnesses must be a doctor, so long as there is no issue of lack of mental capacity.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: And I believe that for Question No 76, which I have raised, it is about the fact that doctors are not allowed to ask their patient, "Have you signed the AMD?".

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
text: I hope to receive the Minister of State's reply to that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the second point, actually, I did mention it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: You would appreciate the seriousness of the implications of an AMD.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But if there is any further feedback in specific circumstances, feel free to raise it to us and we can look at how we can continue to improve the process as we are reviewing this.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: I just want to assure you that I fully agree that there is a time and place to ask that question, whether an AMD has been executed and it should not be done at insensitive junctures where the circumstances have not arisen for an AMD to be relied upon.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: But to the question of confidentiality, I do think that when you are in a position to ask the patient himself or herself, there should not be a concern that there is an issue of confidentiality, because you are asking that information from the patient.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: But currently, the doctors are not even allowed to do that.

speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
text: So, I hope there would be some interest in trying to remove that requirement, but of course, re-affirm that it must still be information that is sought at the appropriate time and place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will just reiterate the point I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, in terms of the process, it is something that we have been monitoring and it is something that is done very promptly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is not something that causes any inordinate delay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But like I said, if there are some specific circumstances, please let us know.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this is something that I think does not stop the doctor from having that robust discussion, especially as they also discuss things, like Advanced Care Planning and LPA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They can, indeed, talk about the concept, so that the patient is aware of it and may want to choose it.
